turns: My full and final settlement of Rs 1,35,000 hasn't been paid. I resigned and my last working day was 14 August 2026. I'm a marketing manager at a private company in Mumbai. HR stopped replying to emails after 1 October.

results.reply:
Look, your case is quite straightforward. Your employer is legally in the wrong because they did not settle within 2 working days, and a significant amount of time has passed since then. The HR department's failure to reply is merely a tactic to make you tired and give up. Your case is strong because you likely have an employment record, and the amount is clear.

**My view:** Your claim is strong. According to the law, the final settlement should have been received within 2 working days after resignation. HR's silence does not weaken your case; rather, it shows that they are intentionally withholding payment. Now, we need to increase the pressure.

**Law on your side:**
* According to section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019, if you resign, your full and final settlement should be completed within 2 working days.
* Under section 45 of the Code on Wages, 2019, you can file a claim with the labour authority. You fall under the definition of an 'employee', even if you are a manager.

**What they will say, and your answer:**
* They might say that the 'process is ongoing' or the 'accounts department is busy'. Your answer: "The process cannot take more than 80 days. I need payment confirmation within the next 7 days, otherwise, I will file a formal complaint with the labour authority."

**What I would do:**
Send a formal 'Demand Notice' email to HR and the company directors today. Clearly state in it that the payment was due by 2026-08-17 and has not been received yet. If there is no response or payment within 7 days, we will file a complaint with the labour authority. I can help you draft this notice.

**I need from you:**
Do you have the resignation acceptance email or letter? And do you have any document where the company has confirmed the amount of Rs 1,35,000?

citations.title: Deadline for paying wages, including after leaving the job
citations.plain: Wages are due by these deadlines: daily workers at the end of the shift; weekly workers on the last working day of the week; fortnightly workers before the end of the second day after the fortnight; monthly workers before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If you are removed, dismissed, retrenched or resign, or lose your job because the establishment closes, your wages must be paid within two working days.

citations.title: Filing a wage claim: who decides it and the 3-year limit
citations.plain: Wage claims under the Code are heard by an authority the Government appoints, who must be at least a Gazetted Officer. The claim can be filed by you, your registered trade union, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator. File within 3 years of the date the claim arises; a later claim may still be accepted if you show sufficient cause. Besides the amount due, the authority can award compensation of up to ten times the claim, and it tries to decide within three months.

citations.title: No salary ceiling for the timely-payment and deduction rules
citations.plain: The old Payment of Wages Act protected only employees earning up to Rs 24,000 a month. Under the Code on Wages, the rules on paying wages on time and on permitted deductions apply to all employees, whatever their salary. The labour ministry has confirmed that this includes white-collar staff.
